en: 2. The Question on the Lotus Parts “Venerable Nāgasena, when you say that ‘three parts of the lotus are to be adopted,’ which are those three parts to be adopted?
“Just as, Great King, the lotus is born in the water, grows in the water, yet remains unsullied by the water;”
In the same way, Great King, the practitioner of yoga, the yogāvacara, must remain entirely unsullied by family, group, gain, fame, honor, respect, and the requisites for enjoyment.
This, Great King, is the first quality of the lotus that should be adopted.
Furthermore, Great King, the lotus stands having risen up above the water.
In the same way, Great King, the practitioner of yoga, having overcome the entire world and risen above it, should stand firm in the supramundane Dhamma.
This, Great King, is the second quality of the lotus that should be adopted.
Furthermore, Great King, even when stirred by a slight breeze, the lotus trembles.
"In the same way, Great King, a practitioner of yoga, a follower of the holy life, must exercise restraint even toward minor defilements and should dwell seeing them as a danger.
This, Great King, is the third quality of the lotus that should be adopted.
And this was said, Great King, by the Blessed One, the God beyond Gods: 'Seeing danger in even the slightest faults, he trains himself by undertaking the rules of training.'"
The second question: on the lotus-design.
